newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex sees extra potential petroleum reserves.
newsitem.headline: Pemex sees extra potential petroleum reserves.

text.p: Mexico's oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said Thursday the country's potential reserves in the Gulf of Mexico could amount to 100 billion barrels of crude equivalent, in addition to proven reserves of 60 billion barrels.
A Pemex spokeswoman said Pemex E&P head Jose Antonio Ceballos Soberanis made the announcement at an annual national congress of Mexican engineers in Zacatecas earlier Thursday.
His words were summarized in a Pemex press statement. Pemex officials were unable to provide a full text of Ceballos' remarks.

A company spokeswoman who declined to be named told Reuters the 100 billion barrels in potential reserves was in addition to proven reserve levels of 60 billion as of January 1, 1997, and had not been previously announced.
"The Mexican portion of the mega-basin of the Gulf of Mexico has an additional potential of more than 100 billion barrels of crude equivalent," the Pemex statement said.
Ceballos spoke to an audience of engineers about Pemex's exploration strategy through 2001, the spokeswoman said, but gave no further details.

Mexican reserve figures have been questioned in the past by foreign industry analysts. Mexico recently revised down its proven reserves level in the Campeche Sound region -- part of the Gulf of Mexico -- to reflect a new externally audited study method.
